references.text: Aaron shall enter the sanctuary with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering on the Day of Atonement, corresponding to the offerings mentioned in Numbers 29:8.
Describes the tenth day of the seventh month as the Day of Atonement, the same festival to which the offerings in Numbers 29:8 are linked.
The same sacrifice formula with a bull, a ram, and seven one-year-old lambs without defect is used for other festival offerings.
A parallel sacrificial regulation for the Feast of Weeks with the same number of animals: one bull, one ram, and seven lambs.
The same sacrificial instruction for the Feast of Trumpets with burnt offerings of a bull, a ram, and seven one-year-old lambs without defect.
A basic regulation concerning burnt offerings that must be without defect, corresponding to the requirement of 'temimim' (without defect) in Numbers 29:8.
The expression 'a pleasing aroma to the Lord' (reach nichoach) is used for burnt offerings, using the same terminology as in Numbers 29:8.

The book of Hebrews explains that the repeated sacrifices under the law, including the offering on the Day of Atonement, could not make the worshippers perfect but pointed forward to Christ's final sacrifice.
